items.title: CISA, FBI, HHS, USDA, and DOT Urge Critical Infrastructure To Strengthen Industrial Refrigeration and Cold Chain Monitoring Systems Cybersecurity
items.one_liner: Critical infrastructure operators are being warned to secure internet-facing industrial refrigeration systems against cyber threats that could lead to physical damage.
items.summary: CISA, the FBI, and other federal agencies have issued a joint fact sheet warning that malicious actors are targeting vulnerabilities in industrial refrigeration and cold chain monitoring systems. These systems, used across healthcare, food, and agriculture sectors, are being exploited via internet-accessible controllers to potentially cause physical damage, such as fire hazards or inventory loss. The agencies urge organizations to remove these devices from the internet, enforce strong password policies, and retire legacy hardware that is no longer supported by vendors.

items.bottom_line: Organizations relying on industrial refrigeration must immediately audit their internet exposure and patch or replace legacy controllers to prevent physical operational sabotage.

items.title: Claude Code's “Don't Ask Again” File Exposes Passwords and Keys in 1,122 Public Copies on GitHub
items.one_liner: Your AI coding assistant might be committing your production secrets to public git history if you use the 'don't ask again' feature.
items.summary: Anthropic's Claude Code AI assistant is inadvertently leaking sensitive credentials, including database passwords and API keys, by saving them in a local configuration file. When users select the 'don't ask again' option for shell commands, the tool saves the full command string—often containing secrets—into '.claude/settings.local.json'. Security researchers at Apiiro identified 1,122 public GitHub repositories containing these files, with some secrets remaining live for over 200 days. Developers are advised to rotate all credentials that have ever been used with the tool and clean their git history.
items.bottom_line: If you use Claude Code, assume any credential used in an automated command is compromised and rotate it immediately.

items.title: White House Network Appears in Global Residential Proxy Traffic

items.summary: Researchers at Layer3 Intel have identified residential proxy traffic originating from the White House's internal network (AS2650). While there is no evidence of malicious intent by White House staff, the presence of these SDKs poses a significant risk of lateral movement and internal network exposure.

items.title: Attackers Exploit Third-Party Provider to Raid French Bank Crédit Mutuel Arkéa
items.one_liner: A major European banking breach via a third-party service provider underscores supply-chain vulnerabilities in financial institutions.
items.summary: Hackers infiltrated French cooperative bank Crédit Mutuel Arkéa by exploiting a third-party service provider's platform, utilizing the bank's own account to execute fraudulent transactions totaling up to $133 million. The stolen funds were funneled through other banking institutions, converted into USDC and USDT stablecoins, and aggressively swapped for privacy-focused cryptocurrencies like Monero. Although customer assets remained unaffected and operations have gradually resumed, the lack of immediate public disclosure allowed attackers to rapidly launder substantial sums before authorities could freeze them. The Paris prosecutor's cybercrime unit and France's cybercrime police are currently leading an active investigation into the breach, while the bank strengthens its security posture and warns users of heightened phishing risks.

Investigating agency: Paris prosecutor's cybercrime unit
items.bottom_line: Financial institutions remain acutely vulnerable to multi-million dollar thefts via compromised third-party vendor platforms rather than direct network breaches.

items.title: CVE-2026-122321 (HIGH 8.5): Kyverno 1.18.0 before 1.19.2 contains a signature verification bypass in verifyImages because cached verifica…
items.one_liner: Kyverno cache poisoning flaw allows attackers to bypass image signature verification via registry tag manipulation.
items.summary: Kyverno versions 1.18.0 through 1.19.1 contain a signature verification bypass vulnerability in verifyImages due to cached results being keyed by image reference strings rather than verified digests. Attackers who can submit workloads and manipulate a registry tag can cause cache hits that skip signature checks, subsequently using mutateDigest to pin the unverified digest. The vulnerability carries a CVSS base score of 8.5.
items.bottom_line: Kubernetes environments running vulnerable Kyverno versions must upgrade to 1.19.2 immediately to prevent unauthorized workload admission via cache bypass.

items.title: Cisco Informational for Emergency Distrust of eMudhra Root and Intermediate Certificate Authorities
items.one_liner: Cisco issued an informational advisory regarding the emergency distrust of eMudhra intermediate CAs due to weak key generation.
items.summary: Between October 17 and October 20, 2026, a critical security compromise was uncovered involving Certificate Authorities managed by eMudhra. A security researcher demonstrated that private keys for eight eMudhra intermediate certificates were fundamentally broken due to an error in their Key Generation Ceremony in April 2025, enabling anyone to brute-force acquire the private keys within seconds. Cisco issued an informational security advisory regarding the emergency distrust of these eMudhra root and intermediate certificate authorities across products. Similar advisories have been published by Cisco Talos and Splunk.

items.title: USN-8955-2: nginx vulnerabilities
items.one_liner: Ubuntu backports critical nginx security patches addressing regex map directive flaws and denial-of-service vulnerabilities.
items.summary: Ubuntu has issued security updates via USN-8955-2 to fix critical vulnerabilities in nginx across older releases including Ubuntu 20.04 LTS, 18.04 LTS, 16.04 LTS, and 14.04 LTS. items.one_liner: A critical path validation flaw in Kyverno allows namespaced CEL policies to achieve full cluster takeover.
items.summary: Kyverno versions 1.16.0 before 1.19.2 contain a critical vulnerability where resource.get() and resource.post() fail to validate path segments in resource arguments. The vulnerability carries a CVSS base score of 9.4.
items.bottom_line: Administrators must update Kyverno immediately to prevent privilege escalation and cluster takeover via malicious CEL policies.

items.title: Fake security tools on GitHub push backdoors and infostealers
items.one_liner: Security researchers are being targeted by malicious GitHub projects that use advanced in-memory evasion to deploy backdoors and steal credentials.
items.summary: A long-running campaign is targeting cybersecurity professionals by distributing malicious GitHub repositories disguised as legitimate security tools. The malware, which has compromised over 2,000 Windows systems, uses sophisticated evasion techniques including patching AMSI and ETW in memory to avoid detection. The final payload includes the AsyncRAT backdoor, clipper malware, and an information stealer that exfiltrates browser data and credentials via Telegram. Researchers note the threat actor is actively improving the loader's capabilities, suggesting a persistent and evolving threat.
items.bottom_line: Do not execute unverified security scripts or tools from GitHub without rigorous sandboxing, as they may contain sophisticated backdoors designed to bypass Windows security features.

items.title: Chainalysis says breach exposed credentials for all customers
items.one_liner: Chainalysis has taken its entire platform offline following a breach that exposed credentials and API tokens for all customers.
items.summary: Blockchain intelligence firm Chainalysis suffered a breach where attackers used 'offensive agentic techniques' to access customer credentials and live tokens. The incident, initially described as limited to metadata, escalated to include the exposure of usernames and password hashes for all users via a Man-in-the-Middle attack. The company has taken its login portal and core products, including Reactor and Data Solutions, offline to harden systems. Customers are now required to provide trusted IP addresses to regain access and must rotate all credentials and API keys.
key_facts: Exposed: Usernames, password hashes, live tokens
Attack vector: Offensive agentic techniques / MITM
items.bottom_line: If you use Chainalysis tools, assume your API keys and credentials are compromised and must be rotated immediately upon portal restoration.

items.title: Japan Announces Emergency Cybersecurity Package Following a Wave of Attacks
items.one_liner: Japan is launching a $63 million emergency cybersecurity initiative to counter rising AI-powered threats.
items.summary: Japan has announced a 10 billion yen ($63 million) emergency cybersecurity package to combat a surge in AI-driven attacks against government agencies and major corporations. The initiative includes the formation of a 'top gun' team of experts to use AI for network defense, the deployment of a 'cyber rescue team' for incident response, and the implementation of 'active cyber defense' measures. This move follows a series of high-profile data breaches affecting millions of records across various sectors.
items.bottom_line: Japan is formalizing its 'active cyber defense' strategy and investing heavily in AI-driven security teams to mitigate the impact of widespread data breaches.

items.title: ZDI-26-880: OriginLab Origin Viewer OGWU File Parsing Stack-based Buffer Overflow Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
items.one_liner: A stack-based buffer overflow in OriginLab Origin Viewer allows remote code execution via a malicious OGWU file.
items.summary: A stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability exists in OriginLab Origin Viewer due to improper length validation when parsing OGWU files. Remote attackers can exploit this flaw by tricking a target into opening a malicious file, leading to arbitrary code execution in the context of the current process. OriginLab has released software updates to address the issue.
items.bottom_line: Users must update OriginLab Origin Viewer to prevent remote code execution through crafted OGWU files.

claims.text: This vulnerability allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of OriginLab Origin Viewer.

items.title: DigiCert admits 16-month security lapse exposed customer information
items.one_liner: A major certificate authority suffered a massive data breach due to a botched server migration and poor internal access controls.
items.summary: DigiCert exposed sensitive customer data, including passports and driver's licenses, for 16 months due to a misconfigured server migration. An internal system was moved to a public-facing availability zone without proper security controls, allowing unauthorized users to create accounts and access archived records. The company discovered the breach in June 2026 but failed to fully investigate or secure the system until months later.
items.bottom_line: DigiCert's failure to secure an internal system during a migration exposed high-value identity documents, highlighting critical gaps in their internal security posture.

items.title: Hacking on Autopilot: Inside ARTEX Cybercrime Campaigns
items.one_liner: The proliferation of autonomous 'agentic' hacking frameworks like ARTEX significantly lowers the barrier to entry for large-scale, automated exploitation.
items.summary: ARTEX is an open-source, AI-powered penetration testing platform that enables autonomous, large-scale cyberattacks. Threat actors use the tool to coordinate AI agents that discover and exploit vulnerabilities, such as RCE, with minimal human intervention. Despite the developer closing the source code following attacks on South Korean banks, numerous forks remain active, and researchers have identified over 1,600 publicly exposed instances of the platform.
items.bottom_line: The shift toward fully autonomous, AI-driven exploitation platforms means attackers can now scale operations without requiring deep technical expertise.

items.title: Zyxel Switch Patch Missed Flaw Behind Wave of Attacks
items.one_liner: A supposed security patch for Zyxel GS1900 switches left an unauthenticated root RCE flaw completely unmitigated, requiring another round of firmware updates.
items.summary: Firmware security company Binarly discovered that a security update released by Zyxel in June failed to fix a critical out-of-bounds write vulnerability in its GS1900 switches, leaving ten models vulnerable to remote root code execution. The flaw, now assigned CVE-2026-107441 with an 8.8 to 9.8 CVSS score, allows unauthenticated attackers to run OS commands via the web management interface. Binarly found that all ten firmware releases advertised as the June fix still contained the vulnerable code because the added security check executed only after the unsafe memory copy occurred. Zyxel has since confirmed the issue, released new firmware versions across the affected models in October, and advised users to apply the updated patches immediately.

CVE-2026-7273: CVSS 8.8, stack-based buffer overflow fixed on June 16
Initial attack scale: 996 switches across 48 countries
items.bottom_line: Do not trust that a previous vendor patch fixed your Zyxel GS1900 switches; all ten firmware releases from the June fix remain vulnerable to CVE-2026-107441 and require an immediate update.

items.title: Anthropic won't fix a Claude Dispatch flaw that could let attackers execute remote commands across corporate boundaries
items.one_liner: Anthropic declined to patch a high-risk architecture flaw in Claude Dispatch and Cowork that allows browser extensions to trigger remote code execution.
items.summary: Security researcher Gal Weizman discovered that Anthropic's Claude Dispatch feature and API are reachable from regular logged-in web sessions, allowing an arbitrary browser extension to make Claude Desktop execute arbitrary code on a user's machine. Despite disclosing the flaw known as 'ThisBash' in May and highlighting that it affects subsequent features like Claude Cowork and Claude Code Remote Control, Anthropic declined to fix the underlying design issue or issue a bug bounty. Anthropic instead planned to retire Dispatch by late October, though the feature remained partially available in limited beta. Weizman warns that the fundamental vulnerability persists across newer cloud-to-desktop session sharing designs.
items.bottom_line: Relying on web session access for desktop agent execution introduces severe privilege escalation vectors if third-party browser extensions are compromised.

claims.text: A vulnerability in Anthropic’s Claude products lets any browser extension that can control Claude Dispatch make Claude Desktop run code on the computer – or even a different machine signed into the same Claude account – with no browser exploit and minimal user interaction required.

items.title: The SOC Files 5: Ghost in the pipeline, or a fileless SharePoint breach by Storm-2603
items.one_liner: Storm-2603 weaponized CVE-2025-53770 in Microsoft SharePoint, maintaining fileless access via the IIS worker process.
items.summary: Retrospective analysis of an attack on on-premises Microsoft SharePoint servers revealed that threat actor Storm-2603 used the IIS worker process (w3wp.exe) as a fileless, memory-resident access bridge. The intrusion began on December 20 with vulnerability fingerprinting using ONYPHE to probe for CVE-2025-53770 (ToolShell), followed by a three-day tactical silence. On December 24, the full RCE chain was executed over HTTP to establish persistent memory-resident access before subsequent ransomware deployment.
items.bottom_line: Attackers can leverage the IIS worker process for memory-resident persistence on SharePoint servers, evading traditional disk-based detection.

claims.text: In 2025, several threat actors exploited CVE-2025-53770 and CVE-2025-53771 (ToolShell vulnerabilities) in on-premises Microsoft SharePoint to achieve remote code execution through crafted HTTP requests.

items.title: CVE-2026-0316 PAN-OS: Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) Vulnerability (Severity: LOW)
items.one_liner: CVE-2026-0316 exposes Palo Alto PAN-OS management web interfaces to stored XSS via malicious authenticated administrators.
items.summary: A stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-0316 with a CVSS base score of 4.8, affects Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS software on PA-Series, VM-Series, and Panorama appliances. The flaw allows a malicious authenticated administrator to store or execute JavaScript payloads through the web interface. Risk is minimized when management interfaces are restricted to trusted internal IP addresses or jump boxes. Palo Alto Networks reports no active malicious exploitation and has issued software updates addressing vulnerable versions across PAN-OS 11.1, 11.2, 12.1, and 12.2 branches.
key_facts: Affected Products: PAN-OS on PA-Series, VM-Series, and Panorama
items.bottom_line: Administrators must patch PAN-OS or strictly isolate management interfaces to internal IPs to mitigate CVE-2026-0316 stored XSS risks.

items.title: A Series of Unauthenticated Events: Chained Exploitation of Ivanti Connect Secure Zero-Days
items.one_liner: This critical vulnerability chain highlights the ongoing risk of VPN appliances as entry points for credential theft and lateral movement.
items.summary: Threat actor UTA0576 exploited a zero-day vulnerability chain in Ivanti Connect Secure (ICS) VPN appliances to achieve unauthenticated root-level code execution. The chain included an authentication bypass (CVE-2026-104935), a file write vulnerability, and a privilege escalation vulnerability (CVE-2026-111357). The attacker extracted sensitive credentials, including LAPS passwords and BitLocker keys, while deleting logs to hide their tracks. Ivanti has released patches for these vulnerabilities, and forensic investigation is recommended for any ICS devices showing signs of lateral movement.
items.bottom_line: Organizations using Ivanti Connect Secure must ensure they are fully patched against the CVE-2026-111357 privilege escalation and CVE-2026-104935 RCE chain.

items.title: AI Security Scoping: Define What To Test In Your Deployment
items.one_liner: Organizations should move beyond generic 'AI checks' by aligning security testing methods with specific business risk decisions.
items.summary: Effective AI security scoping requires organizations to define specific risk decisions—such as whether to ship, gate, or mitigate—before selecting a testing methodology. The article warns against treating diverse activities like penetration testing, red teaming, and architecture reviews as a generic 'AI check,' which often leaves operational risks unaddressed. A robust scope must cover the entire stack, including RAG pipelines, agents, identity, and third-party services, with depth increasing as the deployment matures.
items.bottom_line: AI security is a full-stack challenge; effective scoping must map specific testing methodologies to clear business risk decisions to be defensible.

claims.text: AI security scoping starts with the risk decision (ship, gate, expand, or mitigate) and picks the method that can answer it with evidence: AI penetration testing for exploitable technical weaknesses, a GenAI architecture security review for design and controls, AI red teaming for whether the system’s behavior can be manipulated, and traditional red teaming for detection and response across the broader environment.
claims.support_span: AI security scoping starts with the risk decision (ship, gate, expand, or mitigate) and picks the method that can answer it with evidence: AI penetration testing for exploitable technical weaknesses, a GenAI architecture security review for design and controls, AI red teaming for whether the system’s behavior can be manipulated, and traditional red teaming for detection and response across the broader environment.

items.title: Which LLM writes the best code? A 2026 comparison
items.one_liner: A structured pilot framework across seven criteria helps development teams select and manage coding LLMs effectively.
items.summary: Selecting the best LLM for coding requires a structured framework rather than relying on stale public leaderboards, given frequent model releases from Anthropic, Google, OpenAI, and SpaceXAI. Teams should evaluate models across seven core criteria—code correctness, security, maintainability, repository context, latency, cost, and governance—by piloting them directly on internal repositories. According to Stack Overflow's 2026 Developer Survey, roughly 80% of developers use multiple AI coding tools and frequently switch between them. Independent verification via CI quality gates remains essential to catch insecure patterns or maintainability issues regardless of the model chosen.
key_facts: Adoption: ~80% of developers use 2+ AI tools
items.bottom_line: Evaluate coding LLMs using repository-specific pilots and CI checks instead of public leaderboards.

claims.text: Stack Overflow's 2026 Developer Survey showed about 80% of respondents use two or more AI tools for work.
claims.support_span: In Stack Overflow’s 2026 Developer Survey , about 80% of respondents said they use two or more AI tools for work, and about two-thirds said they had switched AI tools during the year.

items.title: New York's Queens Public Library battles ransomware crims: Wi-Fi, checkouts, and website go dark
items.one_liner: A ransomware attack knocked out digital services, Wi-Fi, and check-out systems across Queens Public Library's 66 locations.
items.summary: The Queens Public Library (QPL) in New York City confirmed it is managing a ransomware attack that disabled its website, online catalog, check-out and return machines, public Wi-Fi, mobile app, and digital media services. All 66 library branches remain physically open to patrons, though network restoration will take time, echoing prolonged recovery timelines seen in other public library cyber incidents like that of the British Library. No ransomware group has claimed responsibility for the disruption.
items.bottom_line: Public library networks remain vulnerable to ransomware disruptions that take core digital checkout and web infrastructure offline for extended periods.

items.title: Russian APT29 Targets Mobile Users with Watering Hole Attacks
items.one_liner: APT29 is actively using watering hole attacks and supply-chain compromises to target mobile devices, posing a significant risk to high-profile individuals and government officials.
items.summary: The Russian state-linked threat actor APT29 is conducting a large-scale watering hole campaign targeting mobile users in the US, Ukraine, Bulgaria, and the Czech Republic. The attackers are compromising high-profile websites and a Ukrainian analytics service, Plerdy, to inject malicious scripts that profile and potentially infect visitors. The campaign includes the creation of sophisticated fake websites, such as a proxy for a London luxury hotel, likely intended to target high-value diplomatic delegations. The operation demonstrates a broad effort to compromise mobile devices through both direct website poisoning and supply-chain attacks.
key_facts: Threat Actor: APT29 (Cozy Bear, Nobelium, Midnight Blizzard)
items.bottom_line: Mobile users, particularly those in sensitive government or diplomatic roles, are facing increased risk from sophisticated watering hole attacks that bypass traditional perimeter defenses.

items.title: CVE-2026-124493 - SunEditor before 3.4.0 Stored XSS via DocumentType Header textContent
items.one_liner: A critical XSS vulnerability in SunEditor allows for session hijacking via malicious header content.
items.summary: SunEditor versions prior to 3.4.0 contain a stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the DocumentType constructor. The flaw occurs because header textContent is injected into innerHTML without proper HTML escaping. Attackers can exploit this by storing entity-encoded HTML in h1-h6 headers, which executes arbitrary JavaScript when the editor initializes in document:header mode, potentially leading to session cookie theft.
items.bottom_line: If you use SunEditor, you must update to version 3.4.0 or later immediately to prevent stored XSS attacks.

items.title: Investigating Ephemeral Supply Chain Tampering
items.one_liner: This campaign demonstrates a sophisticated, time-sensitive supply chain attack technique that evades traditional EDR and automated file scanning by using extremely short-lived malicious configurations.
items.summary: Threat actor UNC7017 compromised AOMEI Technology's update infrastructure between April and July 2026 to deliver the CROSSROAD downloader and SHINYROAD backdoor. The attackers used ephemeral, 5-10 minute windows of configuration tampering to inject malicious payloads, effectively bypassing standard automated scanning and point-in-time triage. Impacted organizations were identified across multiple global regions, including India, with the campaign likely affecting any system that polled the update servers during the tampering windows. AOMEI has since implemented corrective security measures following notification from Google Threat Intelligence and the ManageEngine Threat Analysis Lab.

items.title: Mind the (Patch) Gap: Multiple Chinese Threat Actors Chain 0-day Exploits in Chrome & Windows
items.one_liner: Chinese APT groups are actively exploiting a patch gap between upstream Chromium fixes and browser releases via chained 0-days.
items.summary: Volexity detected spear-phishing campaigns in September 2026 by Chinese threat actors UTA0560 and JungleBamboo targeting NGOs using a multi-stage exploit chain. The attacks abused reflected XSS on legitimate websites to redirect victims to a Google Chrome zero-day, CVE-2026-85046, which was unpatched in released browser versions despite upstream fixes in Chromium. The exploit chain leveraged a V8 type-confusion bug (CVE-2026-85046), a WebAssembly sandbox escape (CVE-2026-87491), and a Windows kernel vulnerability (CVE-2026-85880) to deploy malware including the GRIMWEDGE backdoor and SUPERSTOMP loader.
items.bottom_line: Threat actors UTA0560 and JungleBamboo have been observed chaining a Chrome zero-day (CVE-2026-85046) and Windows kernel bug to target NGOs with persistent backdoors.

items.title: GhostMap Bug Leaves Android Phones Stuck in Reboot Loop
items.one_liner: An unpatched Android OS vulnerability called GhostMap forces affected devices into an endless crash loop requiring a full factory reset.
items.summary: Bitdefender discovered a critical Android vulnerability dubbed GhostMap that causes devices to enter an unrecoverable reboot and crash loop when the operating system mishandles specific zip compression fields and uncompressed length parameters. The parsing error triggers a SIGBUS signal in whichever process reads the malformed file, affecting system components, application launchers, and local security tools alike. Because the persistence loop survives standard reboots and safe mode, the only recovery mechanism is a factory reset that destroys local user data. Google has declined to issue a security patch, classifying the bug outside its fix scope.
items.bottom_line: Android's mishandling of malformed zip archive headers can be exploited to permanently brick devices or disable security pipelines without an administrative fix.

items.title: patrick1357/impnxc-cloak — Wire and behavioural de-fingerprinting patches for impacket and NetExec
items.one_liner: A new tool allows red teamers to patch Impacket and NetExec to evade EDR and network monitoring by mimicking legitimate Windows traffic.
items.summary: The impnxc-cloak project provides a set of patches for Impacket and NetExec designed to strip network and behavioural fingerprints that security tools use to detect these frameworks. items.title: How one exported activity in Microsoft Authenticator let an unprivileged app get tokens for any Microsoft service (CVE-2026-80097)
items.one_liner: An exported activity in Microsoft Authenticator allowed unprivileged Android apps to steal enterprise tokens via a flawed signature check.
items.summary: Researchers discovered a high-severity vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-80097 in Microsoft Authenticator for Android, caused by an improperly secured and exported activity. An unprivileged Android app with zero permissions could invoke AccountChooserActivity, spoof the caller UID, and leverage a flawed signature check to obtain valid delegation tokens for any installed first-party Microsoft application like Teams. This granted attackers full delegated access to the victim's work mailboxes, files, and calendar without requiring any user interaction beyond having an active work account signed into the broker. Microsoft has issued a security patch to resolve the issue.
key_facts: Target application: Microsoft Authenticator for Android
items.bottom_line: Android enterprise users and organizations must immediately update Microsoft Authenticator to prevent unprivileged local apps from harvesting high-privilege access tokens.

items.one_liner: A supply-chain compromise via GitHub release swapping on the OVHcloud CLI directly targets developer credential stores, including AI-agent configurations.
items.summary: Attackers compromised five published releases of the official OVHcloud CLI on GitHub by swapping release binaries with a credential stealer between 12:47 and 14:21 UTC on October 19, 2026. The compromise occurred because GitHub release immutability was disabled, allowing a contributor account with write access to replace assets on old releases without triggering CI workflows. The swapped binaries, downloaded around 250 times before removal, targeted local secrets including AI-agent credential stores, cloud CLIs, and SSH keys. OVHcloud has since deleted the assets, shipped an immutable v0.16.0 release, and advised affected users to treat compromised hosts as fully breached.
items.bottom_line: If you ran an OVHcloud CLI binary downloaded from GitHub between 12:47 and 14:21 UTC on October 19, 2026, treat the machine as fully compromised and rotate all secrets.

items.title: CVE-2026-123776: RRD::CGI::Image versions through 0.01 for Perl pass CGI query parameters containting "tz" to tzset(), , so a FIFO or device path blocks the CGI process
items.one_liner: A Perl CGI library vulnerability allows attackers to cause a denial-of-service by passing malicious timezone parameters.
items.summary: A vulnerability in RRD::CGI::Image (versions through 0.01) allows an attacker to block the CGI process by passing a specific query parameter. The library fails to validate the 'tz' parameter before passing it to the tzset() function, which interprets values starting with '/' or ':' as file paths. By providing a path to a FIFO or a blocking device, an attacker can cause the process to stall indefinitely. Users are advised to apply the available patch to fix this input validation flaw.
items.bottom_line: If you use RRD::CGI::Image, you must patch immediately to prevent trivial process-blocking attacks.

items.summary: A SQL injection vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-121265, has been discovered in Perl versions of SQL::Abstract before 2.000003. items.title: Modernising threat hunting: Using Semantic Search to Find Risky AI Agent Behavior
items.one_liner: Semantic vector search over AI agent session logs helps security teams catch risky automated behaviors.
items.summary: Security analysts are exploring vector search and semantic querying over stored AI agent session logs—such as those from Claude Code and Cursor—to detect risky agent behavior that traditional keyword and regex rules miss. Because AI agents dynamically choose actions based on high-level user prompts, individual steps may appear benign while the session as a whole creates security risks, such as accidentally committing sensitive files to public repositories. By embedding interaction turns at ingest and performing semantic similarity searches, teams can flag anomalous workflows for human review without relying on costly per-session LLM evaluations.
items.bottom_line: Vector search over stored AI coding agent sessions enables scalable detection of risky, multi-step agent actions.

items.one_liner: A retrospective look at uncovering a $113,337 Linux kernel privilege escalation flaw in the AF_ALG cryptographic subsystem via unprivileged socket APIs.
items.summary: Security researcher Muhammad Alifa Ramdhan details the discovery of CVE-2025-39964, a critical race condition vulnerability in the Linux kernel's AF_ALG cryptographic subsystem that earned a $113,337 reward via Google's kernelCTF. Exploiting out-of-bounds access stemming from how AF_ALG handles inputs across unprivileged sockets, an ordinary user can escalate privileges to root or achieve container escape. Present in the kernel since 2011, this vulnerability preceded the widely known 'Copy Fail' flaw but highlights the same underlying kernel attack surface.
items.bottom_line: Unprivileged access to the Linux kernel's AF_ALG subsystem harbors deep race condition vulnerabilities capable of full privilege escalation and container escape.

items.title: Forwarded Without Question: How Web Frameworks Overtrust the Forwarded Header https://www.lkoskela.fi/blog/2026-11-05-forwarded-without-question/ @secharvester
items.one_liner: Web frameworks like Rails and Spring often overtrust the RFC Forwarded header, leaving applications vulnerable to IP spoofing.
items.summary: Many popular web frameworks and application servers, including Rails, Spring, and Jetty, read values from the RFC 7239 standard Forwarded request header by default. Because reverse proxies and CDNs frequently pass untrusted client-supplied Forwarded headers straight through to backend applications without modification or sanitization, web applications often overtrust the header. This flaw exposes applications to client IP address spoofing, original host name spoofing, and request protocol manipulation. Developers and administrators must configure reverse proxies to drop untrusted proxy headers and ensure their application stack aligns on trusted headers.
items.bottom_line: Failure to strip untrusted Forwarded headers at the reverse proxy layer leaves backend web applications vulnerable to client IP and host header spoofing.

items.title: HackerSignal: A Multi-Source, CVE-Linked Corpus and Prospective Benchmark for Cyber Threat Intelligence
items.one_liner: HackerSignal aggregates 7.45 million multi-source documents into a CVE-linked corpus and benchmark for cyber threat intelligence.
items.summary: HackerSignal is a newly released public corpus and benchmark designed to assist cyber threat intelligence systems by linking exploit code, advisories, and fix commits to specific vulnerabilities. The platform aggregates 7.45 million deduplicated documents spanning from 1988 to 2026 across 64 public sources, categorized into eight source layers such as hacker forums, bug bounty disclosures, and known-exploited-vulnerability records. The dataset is keyed to a shared CVE identifier space and evaluates models across tasks including CVE linkage retrieval, exploit type classification, and temporal generalization. While structured sources yield high precision, grounding informal hacker forum discussions to CVEs remains a challenging open problem highlighted by the benchmark.
items.bottom_line: HackerSignal provides a massive multi-source corpus of 7.45 million CVE-linked documents to benchmark cyber threat intelligence tools.

items.summary: Some WordPress sites can still be attacked while they install the fix for an actively exploited flaw, according to Umut Bayram, the Picus Security researcher who found it. The update that installs the fix still unpacks its files using the site's old, unpatched code, so an attacker who strikes at the right moment can run code on the server. The researcher advises blocking web access to the site's wp-content/upgrade folder before updating. The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-119977, affects WordPress 4.7 through 7.1.3. During a core update that uses a complete package, WordPress unpacks a copy of the new version into a temporary folder inside wp-content/upgrade.

items.title: OpenSSH Issues Emergency Fix for Flaw Letting Long Passwords Bypass SSH Auth on Alpine Linux
items.summary: Attackers can log in to accounts that have no password, such as SSH key-only accounts, on some Alpine Linux servers running the standard openssh-server package. They need network access to the server, an account name, and a password between 257 and 1,024 bytes long. OpenSSH, which rates the flaw critical, released version 10.6p2 today to block it. items.title: The Port That Does Not Exist - Port 0 is the port you are not supposed to use, so nobody looks there.
items.summary: Ask any program to listen on port 0 and it will hand you a socket on port 47193...or 58037...or whatever the kernel felt like that day. It is the number you pass when you want the operating system to pick one for you. The destination port field is 16 bits wide, and 0x0000 fits in 16 bits as well as anything else does. Nothing on the wire stops a packet from being addressed to port 0. Your tools will refuse it, your browser will block it, and your scanner's default port list skips it, because everyone agrees it isn't a real port.

items.title: MiniMax-AI/mcode-agent-table — BYOB Table Protocol v0.1 and reference implementation: bring your own agent (MiniMax Code and others) to one s
items.summary: English · 中文 mcode-agent-table is the BYOB (Bring Your Own Bot) Table Protocol v0.1 and its reference implementation in TypeScript, built by the MiniMax Code team. Most multi-agent systems put every agent inside one platform: one model, one context, one set of credentials. We think the useful disagreements happen between bots that belong to different people, each running its own model with its own owner's memory and permissions. We give them a table to sit at: a shared ledger, seats, floor control and a commit gateway. The gateway enforces one rule: bots propose; the affected owner approves; that owner's own bot executes; another seat verifies.
